submission.clinical_question: Following a right-hand crush injury, is there a soft-tissue collection, hematoma, or evidence of vascular compromise or other complication of compartment syndrome/fasciotomy?
submission.pre_read_summary: 32-year-old man after a motorcycle collision with prolonged extrication. The order specifies hand trauma; the encounter documents a right-hand crush injury complicated by compartment syndrome requiring fasciotomy, but provides no current hand examination or side on the order. Concurrent severe left lower-leg trauma with acute arterial occlusion on Doppler, treated with embolectomy, is a separate issue. Clarify whether this ultrasound is intended for the right hand or the injured left leg before interpretation.
must_include_findings: Confirm imaged side and exact site of concern; correlate with the right-hand crush injury and fasciotomy
Soft-tissue edema, focal hematoma or other fluid collection, including collection size and location
If Doppler is performed, arterial patency and distal perfusion, including any occlusion or flow abnormality
Visible tendon integrity and any focal traumatic soft-tissue defect; note limitations of ultrasound for fracture and for diagnosing compartment syndrome

differential.diagnosis: Traumatic arterial injury of right wrist or hand

submission.clinical_question: Does the palpable left breast mass have imaging features suspicious for malignancy, and is image-guided biopsy indicated?
submission.pre_read_summary: 29-year-old woman with a self-detected, firm, nontender 2.4-cm left upper-outer-quadrant breast mass, without skin changes or nipple retraction. Current encounter notes describe a suspicious irregular mammographic lesion; core biopsy is pending. Strong family history: sister with bilateral breast cancer at 35 and maternal grandmother with ovarian cancer; an earlier note also reports maternal breast cancer at 45. Childhood Wilms tumor treated with left nephrectomy and abdominopelvic (not documented chest) radiation. Crohn disease treated with adalimumab.
must_include_findings: Location, size, and mammographic morphology of the palpable left breast lesion, including margins and any associated calcifications or architectural distortion
Targeted ultrasound correlation and solid versus cystic composition, if performed
Any additional lesions in either breast and axillary lymph node abnormalities
Skin thickening or nipple retraction, if present
BI-RADS assessment and recommendation for image-guided tissue sampling or further imaging

submission.clinical_question: Is there an acute intracranial or other structural cause of the patient's altered behavior and psychosis?
submission.pre_read_summary: Young man with schizophrenia and prolonged social withdrawal/paranoid delusions, now presenting with 2 weeks of escalating erratic behavior, auditory hallucinations and paranoia. No reported trauma or focal neurologic deficits; vital signs, CBC, CMP and urine toxicology are unremarkable. Head CT ordered to exclude an intracranial cause of apparent AMS; chart documentation states CT shows no abnormality.
must_include_findings: Intracranial mass or mass effect and midline shift
Acute territorial infarction or other conspicuous parenchymal abnormality

differential.diagnosis: Substance- or medication-induced psychotic disorder (less likely with negative urine toxicology)
Psychotic disorder due to a structural intracranial lesion
Encephalitis or other central nervous system inflammation
